subject: Clarify redistribution permissions for OpenForge open-model weights
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Ava Stone <ava@openforge.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify redistribution permissions for OpenForge open-model weights

Hi Ava —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As we get the commercial side lined up, legal asked for one bit of clarity that will determine how we position this with our ISV partners and cloud marketplace integrations:

Can OpenForge confirm whether the published model weights (the v2 release you shared) are allowed to be redistributed by Redwood to our certified partners (ISVs, consultancies, cloud marketplaces) under a standard mutual partner program, provided we: 

- require partners to agree to your downstream use restrictions,
- do not permit further sublicensing beyond the partner scope, and
- surface attribution/notice in the UI and documentation?

Specifically, we need to know:
1) Is redistribution to our partners explicitly permitted in the current OpenForge license draft?
2) If so, are there any limits on which partners (e.g., no hosting providers, or "non-production" only)?
3) Are there data residency or export control clauses we need to propagate to partners?

I attached our proposed MPA redlines to make the ask concrete. If redistribution requires a separate distributor addendum, please indicate the process and timeline so we can map legal and commercial steps.

Appreciate a short confirmation or the exact paragraph we can reference. If it's easier, happy to jump on a 30-min sync with OpenForge legal and our partner-ops team this week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
[Attachment: redwood-mpa-redlines.docx (docx)]

From: Ava Stone <ava@openforge.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: openforge-legal <legal@openforge.ai>, Tina Gomez <tina@orchid-consult.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify redistribution permissions for OpenForge open-model weights

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Short answers up front:

1) Redistribution: OpenForge's current v2 license allows redistribution to "authorized partners" but requires a distributor agreement and a simple vetting step. The core clause is in Section 3.2 of the draft we circulated last month.

2) Partner limits: We generally permit ISVs and consultancies to host and distribute within customer engagements. We draw a line at "public hosting marketplaces" unless a commercial hosting addendum is signed — that restriction is mainly to protect attribution and telemetry requirements.

3) Data/export: The license includes standard export control language; there are no additional residency obligations in the license itself, but some customers require contractual assurances we can pass through.

I'll attach the latest license draft (v2) with the distributor addendum highlighted. Our legal team (copied) suggests two options:
- Option A: sign the distributor addendum now (fast, one-page) — allows Redwood to redistribute under defined constraints.
- Option B: proceed under a per-partner approval flow (slower; OpenForge must approve each partner).

We prefer Option A for platform partners like Redwood to avoid friction — the addendum is largely boilerplate. If Redwood can accept the attribution and telemetry hooks (we've marked them in the draft), we can turn this around in a week with standard signatories.

Would you like OpenForge legal to draft the one-page addendum and circulate? If so, copy me and our counsel and we'll start.

Best,
Ava Stone
Head of Publisher Partnerships, OpenForge Labs
ava@openforge.ai | +1 646-555-2190
[Attachment: OpenForge_License_Draft_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Ava Stone <ava@openforge.ai>, openforge-legal <legal@openforge.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify redistribution permissions for OpenForge open-model weights

Ava / OpenForge legal —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. From Redwood legal's perspective, Option A (distributor addendum) is the cleanest operational path. A couple of suggested edits we'd like to propose to the addendum before sign:

- Limit the telemetry requirement to anonymized usage metrics (no raw PII or customer payload).
- Add a clause allowing Redwood to onboard partners that are "certified by Redwood" without additional OpenForge approval, provided Redwood maintains a partner registry and incident/contact process.
- Clarify that sub-licensing is not permitted (only redistribution for the certified partner's customers).

Draft suggested language for the certification clause (inline):
"Certified Partner Distribution: Redwood may redistribute OpenForge Model Weights to partners that have completed Redwood's certification process and agreed to OpenForge's downstream terms. Redwood will provide OpenForge with a quarterly registry of certified partners and notify OpenForge on any security incidents involving redistributed weights."

If OpenForge legal can work with that form, we can accept the addendum and move to signatures. If helpful, Tina Gomez from Orchid (copied) can act as neutral counsel to expedite wording.

--Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-mpa-redlines.docx (docx)]

Vanessa here — next steps proposed:
1) OpenForge legal to draft the one-page distributor addendum (Option A) incorporating Dylan's certification clause and the anonymized telemetry language.
2) Redwood will circulate a short partner certification checklist (security attestation + partner T&Cs) and a registry template.
3) Schedule a 30-min legal sync (Tue or Wed) to finalize language. Vanessa / Dylan / Marissa from our side will attend.

Can OpenForge propose times? If you prefer, we can share a Google Doc with inline redlines before the sync.

Appreciate the quick progress — moving this to an addendum vs per-partner approvals will materially reduce time-to-revenue for both sides.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
